fullPassage:
We meet many people and build many friendships. We sometimes meet remarkable individuals who sacrifice themselves for those in need. It's their daily routine to help others, and they even put others before themselves. Sister Carla is an excellent example of such a person. Often called the angel with blue eyes, she devoted her life to caring for patients with Hansen's disease in the remote village of Hoam, Gochang, Jeollabuk-do.
Born in Bernezzo, Italy in 1943, Sister Carla became a nun at the age of 19 and ended up caring for more than 120 war orphans. "I thought that instead of starting a family and caring for my own children only, I could devote my life to caring for more children." She added, "I also became a nun because I wanted to fulfill the dream of my late brother, who wanted to become a priest but passed away before he could."
The 25-year-old Sister Carla came to Korea in 1968 after hearing about many war orphans and Hansen's patients in Korea. Back then, people excluded Hansen's patients from the general public due to various prejudices. People falsely believed that Hansen's disease was highly contagious, and also felt uncomfortable with the appearance of Hansen's patients. Nowhere was the place for those patients, and their miserable lives were passed on to their own children. For Sister Carla, however, Hansen's patients were equally noble human beings. She accepted the pain of those patients as her own.
Sister Carla wanted to help the Hansen's patients in as many ways as she could. She raised pigs with the patients to help them become economically independent. She started to learn Korean so she could understand each individual's problems more deeply. She struggled with the language at first, but after two years, she was able to communicate with local people freely and truly understand the patients' specific challenges. Additionally, she went to a hospital in Spain to study Hansen's disease and earn a nurse's assistant certification.
When she first began treating Hansen's patients, she was able to treat them with only the small amount of medicine she received from German aid agencies. "The saddest thing at the time was not the fact that there was a lack of medicine, but the prejudice towards the Hansen's patients. Because of that, the children of Hansen's patients were not accepted by normal schools," Sister Carla said. So she founded a school for the children of Hansen's patients in the village. Otherwise, more than a hundred children wouldn't have received proper education.
Her love for the Hansen's patients is also reflected in her Korean name, "Kang Kalla." She adopted the Korean family name "Kang" when the first patient she met at the Hoam Village told her, "I would really like you to use my family name." As her personal name, she decided to use "Kalla," which is the Korean pronunciation of her Catholic name, "Carla."
Sister Carla did her best to be there for anyone who needed her help, but sadly she didn't have enough time to care for herself. She developed rheumatism but didn't treat the disease properly because she was so busy working for her patients. As a result, her toes became severely twisted. Her twisted toes reminded her neighbors of ginger roots, and so they called her toes "ginger feet." She devoted everything she had to the sick, lonely, and poor while she lived very frugally. She wore a 30-year-old watch on her wrist and kept two pencils shorter than her little finger on her desk. Additionally, Sister Carla lived in the same tiny home for over 50 years.
Sister Carla, just like everyone else in Hoam Village, grew old. The beautiful 25-year-old woman aged into a grandma with silver hair. Although many things changed, Sister Carla's desire to sacrifice for others didn't.
In addition to helping the surviving Hansen's patients, she continued to care for the elderly every day. Even in her old age, she took them to the hospital, did their dishes, and took care of problems at the bank for them. She even went grocery shopping for them. She used every bit of her time for those in need. She continued working in the community, running a pottery-making program, and sold pottery to help senior citizens in poor neighborhoods.
When asked how to live a valuable life, she replied: "When you live only for the benefit of yourself, your joy and happiness become that much smaller. But when you open your heart to other people, it changes your life." Sister Carla's extraordinary life reminds us that we all can make a difference and that through our actions we can bring about a positive change in the lives of those who need help most. As she said, being respectful, caring, and supportive towards others can improve our society and also bring us happiness.
It is a volunteer activity that involves reading aloud to the visually impaired or young children. Additionally, you can participate in the production of audiobooks for them. This activity offers the advantage of relatively flexible scheduling. However, participants must meet certain standards, including completing their education and demonstrating proficiency in standard language use and pronunciation.
Adopt-a-tree is a volunteer activity that helps keep trees beautiful and clean. Planting trees is important, but it is also important to take good care of the trees once planted. It is a volunteer activity in which local organizations and residents adopt "my tree" and take care of it and keep it clean. The Seoul Green Trust, a non-profit foundation dedicated to expanding and preserving green spaces, organizes an annual event on Arbor Day. During this event, citizens come together to plant and care for trees along the Hangang River.
Longevity photography is a service aimed at creating healthy and happy memories through pictures for the elderly. It is driven not only by a desire to help the elderly live longer but also to ease their financial burdens. In addition to photography services, you can also contribute through talent donations that match your skills, such as providing makeup or hairstyling for the photo shoots.
In tour guide volunteer work, you provide local information on things like restaurants, shopping options, tourist attractions, and accommodations. Additionally, you may assist with services related to the loss of belongings. In Seoul, for instance, you can participate in guiding tours to major tourist locations, including Myeong-dong, Namdaemun Market, Sinchon, Bukchon, and more.
